solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Not paying attention when former PM returns

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as the clock struck'

indicators.note: returns tells us the prime minister's name is read backwards, coming back the other way

parts.note: Sir Robert Peel was a nineteenth-century British prime minister

explanation.surface: Someone drifts off just as an ex-premier makes a comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Robert Peel was a 19th-century British prime minister; 'returns' reads his surname backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sleeping is in no state to notice anything, so the idiom fits being inattentive.

clue.text: Help Straw on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio means the word is heard spoken rather than seen written down

parts.note: a drinking straw is a sucker, something you suck through

explanation.surface: A request for assistance from a politician named Straw on a broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: Straw looks like the former UK minister Jack Straw; it is a drinking straw, a sucker.
explanation.definitionFit: Succour is assistance given in a time of need, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: The end of Lady in Lake is a high spot

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the name of the lake

parts.note: Lake Erie is one of the North American Great Lakes

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Something about the lady of the lake reaching a lofty perch.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagle's nest built high on a crag is the classic lofty spot.

clue.text: Dislike accommodating son chasing job immediately

indicators.note: chasing means coming behind, so this piece follows the job in the answer

parts.note: a post is a job or position

indicators.note: accommodating means giving room to, so one letter is housed inside the other word

parts.note: to hate is to dislike strongly

explanation.surface: Someone who hates having their son around while chasing a job.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'chasing' means coming below, so the job sits on top; 'accommodating' houses the son inside the dislike.
explanation.definitionFit: Posthaste is an old adverb meaning with the greatest speed, without delay.

clue.text: Scary wild dog almost trapping relation

indicators.note: trapping means holding something inside, so the relative goes within the shortened dog
almost means the word stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: the dingo is Australia's wild dog
an aunt is a family relation

explanation.surface: A frightening feral dog has caught a family member.
explanation.walkthrough: The dingo is Australia's wild dog; 'almost' drops its last letter and 'trapping' puts the relation inside what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Something daunting is intimidating and off-putting, close in meaning to frightening.

clue.text: Indicated study will need books on Labour leader

parts.note: a den is a private room for study
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible
Ed Miliband led the UK Labour Party, so a Labour leader is Ed

explanation.surface: A party chief who will need some reading done in his study.
explanation.definitionFit: To denote is to signify or point out, so it shares the sense of showed.

clue.text: Guide's American idol out of love

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: out of means a letter is removed from the word

parts.note: a hero is someone idolised
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A Girl Guide's American heart-throb falls out of love.
explanation.definitionFit: An usher shows people to their seats, so he acts as a guide.

clue.text: Board accepts one satisfied schedule

indicators.note: accepts means takes in, so the other pieces go inside the board

parts.note: a table is a board, as in a board for meals
I is the Roman numeral one
to have met a need is to have satisfied it

explanation.surface: A committee board approves a single acceptable timetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepts' puts IMET inside TABLE just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A timetable is a schedule of times for events or transport services.

clue.text: Book on anaesthetics?

definitions.meaning: the fourth book of the Old Testament

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the Bible book name; the other reads the word as things that make numb.

clue.text: Plant may crush them in order to protect name

indicators.note: to protect means to surround, so the name letter is shielded inside
in order hints that the letters must be put into a new order

explanation.surface: Gardeners may tread on plants, so order them to shield a name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in order' rearranges MAY CRUSH THEM, and 'to protect' puts N inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: The chrysanthemum is a familiar garden and florist's flowering plant.

clue.text: A bit roughly, I beg your pardon

parts.note: some means approximately, as in 'some fifty people'
what? is a blunt way of asking someone to repeat themselves

explanation.surface: A rough reply when someone asks you to repeat yourself.
explanation.definitionFit: Somewhat means to a modest degree, slightly, just as 'a bit' does.

clue.text: Quite a bit!

definitions.meaning: an adverb meaning fairly, to some degree
the exclamation means 'very much so', an emphatic yes

explanation.definitionFit: The word works both as a mild adverb of degree and as an emphatic exclamation of agreement.

clue.text: Common sense's beginning for people in party

parts.note: a village green is a common, shared open land

indicators.note: beginning means just the first letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Common sense is the first thing members of a political party need.
explanation.walkthrough: Common sense reads as one idea; Common is a village green and only 'sense's beginning' gives S.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Green Party are collectively known by this name in UK politics.

clue.text: Leaves for golf in Arab states

indicators.note: in means this letter is put inside the other word

parts.note: the United Arab Emirates, a federation of Arab states
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone moves abroad to play golf in the Gulf.
explanation.definitionFit: To emigrate is to leave one's own country to settle in another.

clue.text: Information stored at sea — bad planning

indicators.note: planning implies arranging things afresh, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Records kept on board a ship were badly organised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'planning' rearranges AT SEA plus BAD into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A database is a structured collection of data held on a computer.

clue.text: Beefy sends son to the back for accessories

indicators.note: sends means a letter is dispatched to another place in the word
to the back says where it goes: the end of the word

parts.note: strapping means big and strong, beefy

explanation.surface: A burly man packs his son off with all the gear.
explanation.walkthrough: Beefy is also the nickname of cricketer Ian Botham, which the surface plays on; here it just means big and strong.
explanation.definitionFit: Trappings are the outward ornaments or accessories that go with a role or status.

clue.text: Source of gold, for example, in person acting for bully

indicators.note: in tells us this piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a doer is a person who acts
a mine is one source of gold

explanation.surface: Gold, say, lies in someone who stands in for a bully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for example' belongs to the mine, not the bully: a mine is one example of a gold source.
explanation.definitionFit: To domineer is to rule over others arrogantly, which is what a bully does.

clue.text: New car boot sale alas cancelled for this month

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh arrangement of the remaining letters
cancelled says the letters of the sad exclamation are removed from the pool

explanation.surface: A fresh car boot sale has, sadly, been called off this month.
explanation.walkthrough: A car boot sale is a British sale of second-hand goods from car boots (trunks). Take ALAS out of CARBOOTSALE and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: October is the tenth month, here defined by context as the current one.

clue.text: Swindles not working — covered in tears

indicators.note: covered in means one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: rips are tears in fabric
a machine that is off is not working

explanation.surface: A broken-down person ends up weeping.
explanation.walkthrough: Tears suggests crying, but it is rips in cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Rip-offs are frauds or overcharges, which are kinds of swindle.

clue.text: Get retribution in heaven, generally

indicators.note: in tells us the answer lies within the following words

explanation.surface: Divine justice in heaven, as a general rule.
explanation.definitionFit: To avenge a wrong is to exact retribution for it.

clue.text: What may help you look good with girls?

parts.note: lasses is a northern British word for girls

explanation.surface: A man asks what might make him attractive to women.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectacles help the wearer to see, so they aid looking.

clue.text: Road bridge needing something to impart stiffness

parts.note: ST is short for street, a road
an arch is a bridge-like span

explanation.surface: A road bridge needs reinforcement to keep it rigid.
explanation.definitionFit: Starch is used in laundry to stiffen collars and cloth.

clue.text: Animal from hard currency area

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
the yen is Japan's currency

explanation.surface: An animal coming out of a strong-currency zone.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyena is a carnivorous scavenging mammal of Africa and Asia.

clue.text: Conceited person's to pay a call with bird

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay

parts.note: to pop in is to pay a brief visit
the jay is a crow-family bird

explanation.surface: A vain man drops by with his pet bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A popinjay is a vain, foppish person who struts about like a parrot.

clue.text: Rising desire to throttle editor demanding attention

indicators.note: to throttle is to grip round the throat, so one piece encloses another
rising in a down clue means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: a yen is a longing or desire

explanation.surface: A growing urge to strangle a demanding editor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' in a down clue means read upwards, turning the desire round; 'to throttle' makes it grip the editor inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Needy people crave emotional support, constantly seeking attention.

clue.text: Clumsy touches on book, say

parts.note: to utter is to say aloud
to finger something is to touch it with the fingers

explanation.surface: Fumbling hands paw at a book, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'book, say' looks like 'a book, for example'; it is two pieces, B and UTTER. 'on' in an across clue puts the touches after them.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a cry aimed at someone who drops things, standing in for an exclamation of awkwardness.

clue.text: Spring in lock offering access unlawfully

indicators.note: in tells us the spring sits inside the lock of hair

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair
a spa is a mineral spring

explanation.surface: A coiled spring in a door lock lets someone break in.
explanation.walkthrough: Lock suggests a door, but it is a lock of hair, TRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: To trespass is to enter someone's land or property without permission.

clue.text: Most retiring set out after quiet end to party

indicators.note: after means the rearranged letters come behind the other pieces

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet

indicators.note: end to means the last letter of the word
out suggests the letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: The most bashful guests leave once a quiet party winds down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the given word, and 'after' places that result behind the call for quiet and the party's last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Retiring here means shy and reserved, so the superlative is the shyest.
